One treaty in 1763 wiped France's mainland empire off the map of North America. Here it is before and after.

a thread 🧵🗺️
1/ In 1754 (bottom map) France holds a huge swathe of the continent: Canada plus Louisiana. By 1763 (top map) there is no France on the mainland at all.

2/ The Treaty of Paris, signed 10 February 1763, had France give Canada and Cape Breton to Britain and drop its claims to Acadia and Nova Scotia. France kept fishing rights off Newfoundland and got Saint-Pierre and Miquelon back.
3/ The Mississippi became the dividing line. Britain took the land east of it. The west went to Spain, which France had secretly given Louisiana to in the Treaty of Fontainebleau months earlier.
4/ Spain paid for losing the war: it handed Florida to Britain. In exchange, Britain returned Havana and Manila, which it had captured.
5/ Britain also gave Guadeloupe and Martinique back to France, while France recognised British control of Dominica, Grenada, Saint Vincent and Tobago.
6/ Britain looks like the big winner on the 1763 map. Within two decades it would lose its thirteen colonies in a war the new borders helped set up.
Was this Britain's greatest win or the start of its biggest loss? Follow @forummapping for more maps like this.
